before: Existing data centers unaffected unless they cease operations 60+ days or let a business license lapse.
after: The resolution exempts issuance of business licenses to currently operating businesses, unless operation ceases for 60 days or more or an expired license was not timely renewed. This is not an established blanket exemption from all permitting/development restrictions.

before: 180 days from the March 3, 2026 adoption/vote date, expiring August 30, 2026 (March 3 plus 180 days). WBRC and Birmingham Times both confirm the March 3, 2026 vote date and the six-month term; no separate publication-date lag was found or is needed for this calculation.
after: A 180-day suspension was reported after the March 3, 2026 vote. The original executed ordinance, effective-date anchor and actual termination date have not been established; August 30 arithmetic from the vote date is not an accepted operative endpoint.

before: Replaced; the moratorium ended at the close of its 180-day term (on or about 2026-08-30) and was superseded by the permanent data-center zoning ordinance (zoning case ZAC2026-00001, 20 conditions for hyperscale facilities) adopted 6-3 on 2026-06-09, which per WBRC took effect when the moratorium lifted. AL.com (2026-09-18) lists Birmingham's moratorium as expired and replaced by the new zoning regulations; the city's data-center page now describes only the adopted zoning rules.
after: June 9, 2026 reporting describes adoption of permanent data-center zoning. A July 16, 2026 secondary report says the initial March pause had been lifted. [VERIFY: original effective date, exact lifting date, legal transition and current status remain unresolved.]

before: Applies prospectively to new or expanding large/hyperscale data centers above 20 MW. The Nebius BHM01/Oxmoor project and DC BLOX expansion were reported as exempt because applications or permits were already complete or under review before the moratorium took effect.
after: June reporting describes a Nebius exemption from the successor zoning ordinance; it does not establish exemptions from the original moratorium. The original pause scope, size threshold and claimed Nebius/DC BLOX exemptions remain unverified.

before: Replaced by permanent data-center zoning regulations (ZAC2026-00001) adopted 2026-06-09 and effective when the moratorium ended (~2026-08-30).
after: Permanent data-center zoning was reported adopted June 9, 2026; the exact moratorium termination date and legal transition to those regulations remain unresolved.

before: Companion utility-contract review bill. Captured engrossed text would add PSC review criteria for contracts with large load data center customers, including incremental cost recovery and benefits to other customers.
after: Engrossed proposal would add public-interest review criteria for retail electric service contracts with large-load customers, including incremental cost recovery and positive benefits to other customers. Its large-load-customer definition uses expected peak demand of 100 MW or greater at one or more contiguous parcels and is not confined to data processing centers. The text separately uses the term large load data center customer in the incremental-cost definition; that wording difference is not silently normalized.
